ety.text: From ballet + -manie. Although the spelling balletomanie is the most common nowadays, the spelling ballettomanie may be justified by analogy with other derivatives of nouns ending in the diminutive suffix -et, which commonly insert an additional t before vowel-initial suffixes (for example, sonnettiste, motettiste, juillettiste, cornettiste, flageolettiste, galoubettiste). Indeed, ballet derives from Italian balletto, a diminutive of ballo, formed with the Italian suffix -etto, which is a cognate of the French suffix -et (both deriving from the Late Latin suffixe -ittus or -ettus).
Attested in Saint Beauzelly outre Gardon on the Cassini map (1740s).
